cards.design_implication: If designing a DNA data storage system based on enzymatic synthesis, consider using template-independent polymerases like TdT under kinetically controlled conditions to encode information via nucleotide transitions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Here, we describe a de novo enzymatic synthesis strategy designed for data storage which harnesses the template-independent polymerase terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) in kinetically controlled conditions. Information is stored in transitions between non-identical nucleotides of DNA strands.
limitations: Abstract-level claim only; does not establish specific kinetic parameters or enzyme concentrations.
Does not establish the stability or error profile of this mechanism under all conditions.
cards.statement: The source describes a de novo enzymatic synthesis strategy for data storage that uses terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) in kinetically controlled conditions, where information is encoded in transitions between non-identical nucleotides.

cards.design_implication: If implementing iterative nucleotide addition for storage, consider incorporating apyrase-mediated degradation to control the length of homopolymeric extensions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: To produce strands representing user-defined content, nucleotide substrates are added iteratively, yielding short homopolymeric extensions whose lengths are controlled by apyrase-mediated substrate degradation.
limitations: Abstract-level claim only; does not define the concentration or timing of apyrase application.
Does not establish the maximum or minimum effective homopolymer lengths.
cards.statement: The synthesis process involves iterative addition of nucleotide substrates to produce short homopolymeric extensions whose lengths are controlled by apyrase-mediated substrate degradation.
